name: Benjamin Haddad
bio: Benjamin Haddad (born 23 October 1985 in the 16th arrondissement of Paris, into a Sephardic Jewish family of Tunisian origin) is a French politician and foreign-policy specialist. A graduate of Sciences Po Paris (MA in international affairs) and HEC Paris (MA in financial economics), he spent roughly seven years in Washington think tanks, notably as a fellow at the Hudson Institute (2014/2016-2018/2019) and as senior director of the Atlantic Council's Europe Center (2019-2022). He authored 'Le paradis perdu : L'Amérique de Trump et la fin des illusions europeennes' (2019). An early member of Emmanuel Macron's En Marche movement (2016), he was elected to the National Assembly in 2022 for Paris's 14th constituency (covering most of the 16th arrondissement), re-elected in 2024, and chaired the French-Ukrainian parliamentary friendship group. He was appointed Minister Delegate for European Affairs in September 2024 in the Barnier government and retained the post through the Bayrou and successive Lecornu governments, including after the 26 February 2026 reshuffle, serving under Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot.
